rationale: Round 1 built, ran, and preserved correctness with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up while respecting that the program is a tiny, hot-loop-dominated matrix benchmark: mmult dominates runtime, so FLA keeps the highest RuntimeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights (flattening its inner loops would cost the most for the least gain), while BCF stays aggressive but with a moderate runtime brake so bogus predicates still land in the cold ackermann/zeromatrix/freematrix-style functions; SUB, IBR, and SPLIT are near-free instruction-level and basic-block diversifiers and get the strongest security/diversity weights to maximize structural change across all 7 functions; ICALL and IGV add call-site and inter-block indirection that yields good diversity on a program this small without measurable size pressure given only ~2.9KB of text, leaving ample headroom under any size budget; all CorrectnessRisk weights stay at or below 0.3 to preserve the round-1 correctness guarantee while still admitting every pass into consideration.
